brief:
The destruction of Gaza's court system has stripped Palestinian women of legal pathways to secure inheritance, divorce, alimony and property rights, Drop Site News reported. Women navigating the humanitarian crisis face compounding obstacles as judicial institutions collapse, leaving them without means to resolve family disputes or protect assets.

The breakdown occurs as Palestinians in Gaza struggle to survive amid ongoing conflict. Women seeking formal legal remedies for inheritance claims, divorce proceedings and financial support now confront seemingly insurmountable bureaucratic barriers alongside the immediate challenges of displacement and resource scarcity.
dek: As they struggle to survive a genocide, Palestinian women in Gaza face seemingly insurmountable legal and bureaucratic obstacles to secure rights to inheritance, divorce, alimony, property and more.
title: Gaza court collapse leaves women without legal recourse for basic rights
